title: Financial indicators declare units and economic applicability
question: Ratios, percentage outputs, heuristics and pricing models are separate rule candidates, with explicit denominators and rounding.

evidence.title: Named financial ratios carry distinct applicability and rounding policies
explanation: The named ratios and heuristics return different units and rounding: some percentages, some ratios, rounded prices and a72/rate doubling heuristic.
Reading each helper shows no common economic validation or output-unit contract. Recurrence of ordinary number values cannot establish interchangeable financial meaning.

Operation-specific nonzero denominators and meaningful economic inputs; percentage/scalar choices must follow the actual helper. R72 is a heuristic and CAPM returns a scalar while ROI returns percentage; a test name cannot substantiate a different function it does not call. No upstream execution. The cited source branches and expressions were read; floating accuracy, actual resolved dependency versions and economic correctness are not certified. Prior R1-M1 dependency contracts are reused only within their recorded bounds. This behavior is not currently defined by FinKore Core.

evidence.title: Earnings-per-share controls depend on weighted exposure and dilution choices
explanation: Basic EPS uses caller weighted shares; was weights month counts by12. Diluted EPS makes one conditional recomputation and the option helper rejects price<=exercise.
The source does not independently assess each instrument anti-dilution effect or establish an accounting disclosure standard.

Nonzero economically meaningful share denominators, aligned month/share inputs and caller interpretation of tax and convertible instruments. The single recomputation can remain distinct from instrument-by-instrument anti-dilution analysis; out-of-money options raise instead of returning zero incremental shares. No upstream execution. evidence.title: Financial result units and rounding differ across named calculators
explanation: IAR, CAPM, WACC, stockPV, DF and CI expose distinct output units, rounding and time observations despite sharing native number types.
The bodies explicitly scale IAR by100, CAPM inputs by100 without output scaling, WACC to tenths of a percentage point, stockPV to integers, and DF to upward-rounded factors.

Per-function economic domain and denominator conditions; no currency protocol or exact decimal result is asserted. DF excludes its loop endpoint and includes exponent0; CI includes principal rather than interest alone. Equal numeric result types cannot erase those distinctions. No upstream execution.
